citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The attending veterinarian (AV) has not visited the facility on an annual basis, as written in the program of vet care.
During this inspection, the licensee told the inspector the AV visited the facility during the 2026 calendar year but was
unsure of the date. When the inspector contacted the AV, they stated they’ve never visited the facility at the current
location, or the prior address in Chester, South Carolina. At the time of this inspection, the AV hasn’t been scheduled to
visit the facility since the licensee initially contacted them in 2024.
Consistent, regularly scheduled visits by the veterinarian provide a measure of quality assurance and helps sustain
satisfactory oversight and communication by the vet with the facility. The facility shall employ an attending veterinarian
under formal arrangements. In the case of a part-time attending veterinarian or consultant arrangements, the formal
arrangements shall include a written program of veterinary care and regularly scheduled visits to the premises of the
facility.
Correct by October 10, 2026.

The facility did not have acquisition records for two marmosets and one mini-pig. Additionally, no disposition records were
available for the same mini-pig. Though the licensee stated the marmosets housed at the facility are personal pets, the
primates are on display to the public during the reptile tours.
Acquisition and disposition records, including offspring born at the facility, are necessary to accurately track and identify
animals being used in regulated activities, as well as aid in the detection of movement of animals upon relocation to a new
site. The licensee shall make, keep, and maintain records of acquisition/disposition of all animals that fully and correctly
disclose the required information, as outlined in this section.
Correct by September 26, 2026.

citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
The facility does not have a written primate enrichment program for the marmosets housed at the facility. Three
marmosets are housed in the back area of the pet store where guided reptile tours occur. While the licensee stated the
marmosets are personal pets that remain at the pet store, they are housed in the same room as the reptiles included in
the tour and remain on display to the public as the tour is being conducted. During this inspection, a facility representative
confirmed they’d conducted reptile tours while the marmosets were housed in the back room.
Implementing documented enrichment protocols ensure adequate provisions are in place to promote the psychological
well-being of the non-human primates at the facility as directed by the attending veterinarian. The facility must develop,
document, and follow an appropriate plan for environmental enhancement adequate to promote the psychological well-
being of nonhuman primates. The plan must be in accordance with the currently accepted professional standards as cited
in appropriate professional journals or reference guides, and as directed by the attending veterinarian. This plan must be
made available to APHIS upon request.
Correct by October 10, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee and facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
